A and B are 19 arcsec apart, one pixel at default framing: a click picks 'A or B'. B is selectable by id (--map=HIP 71681), by zoom, and in the tour capture, so the criterion holds, but a player cannot choose B from the default view.

sirius_b_recommendation.recommendation: Yes, give Sirius B the system-parallax override, as alpha Cen B got. Sirius is the map's second named destination (replay golden target) and a bright named pair a player will compare. Offset is 0.108 ly (6,800 AU) for a real ~20 AU pair. Caveat: Sirius B is a Gaia/GCNS row in the quick tier, not a HIP bright-tier row, so the existing bright_overrides.json rule (c) mechanism cannot carry it. Needs an override applied in the quick/medium path (set the component's distance to its primary's, keeping its own direction at the shared epoch).
sirius_b_recommendation.wider_scope: The defect is systemic. Within 25 ly there are also Luyten 726-8 A/B 0.092 ly apart at 2.3 arcsec, Wolf 424 A and its companion 0.481 ly at 1.1 arcsec, and pairs at 16.6 ly (0.18 ly). Across the whole 25 pc map, 422 row pairs are within 30 arcsec of each other and 269 of those differ by more than 0.05 ly. A one-star override fixes Sirius; a rule (companion within N arcsec of a brighter row takes that row's parallax, with a ruling like D-19) fixes the class. Suggest: override Sirius B now (cheap, visible), open a decision for the general rule, and cover Luyten 726-8 and Wolf 424 with it.
